Associated Keywords: autoblogging tools, automated blog writing software, ai content automation, autoblogging comparison
Friction: This category quotes prices in four units that cannot be compared: per article, per credit, per tracked prompt, and per connected site. Every roundup lists the headline dollar figures side by side as though they measure the same thing, so the ranking a buyer reads is an artifact of which unit each vendor happened to pick. Compounding it, a large share of the roundups ranking for this query are published by vendors who appear in their own lists.
Logic: Do the conversion the roundups skip, then hand over the method rather than a ranking. Normalized to cost per published article at monthly list rates: Arvow runs about $0.99 bare and about $2.60 for illustrated long-form because its credit pool also pays for images and site optimization; Outrank $3.30 and BabyLoveGrowth $3.30 at its promotional rate; Byword $3.96; Frase $4.90 with 50 audit pages attached; Scalenut $11.80 at list and $2.40 on its promotional annual. RightBlogger cannot be expressed per article at all — it meters sites, not output. Two structural cautions the unit conversion exposes: credit pools shift cost with article shape, and promotional annual rates reverse at renewal. We do not sell autoblogging software, which is why this page ranks nothing and converts nothing — it gives the arithmetic and the disclosure test instead.
content_angle: The category-closing page for the alternatives cluster: instead of a tenth ranked list, it converts four incompatible billing units into one cost-per-published-article figure using first-party prices verified across nine prior comparisons, and gives readers a disclosure test for the vendor-authored roundups that dominate this SERP. States plainly that we sell no product in this category and rank nobody.
author: Marcus Orion
